newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious were called to open lower on Wednesday, with gold's rally stalling due to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's view that inflation was modest, dealers said.
Greenspan, who made the comments in his twice-yearly testimony to Congress on Tuesday, said U.S. economic growth was slowing. Financial markets roared higher in delight.
COMEX August gold was called to open $1.00 to $1.50 an ounce weaker from Tuesday's close at $326.40.
Gold was fixed in London Tuesday morning at $324.35, down from $328.25 on Tuesday afternoon.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks rose 70,285 ounces to 917,005 ounces Tuesday, while COMEX silver stocks fell 163,299 ounces to 176,592,679 ounces.
COMEX September silver was called 2.0 to 3.0 cents lower from Tuesday's finish of $4.303 after trading from $4.32 to $4.275 on ACCESS.
NYMEX October platinum was called $1.50 to $2.00 beneath Tuesday's close of $409.20, with NYMEX September palladium called unchanged from the previous close of $180.00.
